title: Install lib32 graphics drivers before Steam
head: 65883c389082
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An undetected Intel/AMD GPU now falls through to Steam's default NVIDIA provider
leads.consequence: A 3D-only AMD or Intel display controller has class 03:02, not 'VGA'/'Display'; similarly, a machine with an Intel/AMD GPU can be missed when lspci fails or is unavailable from PATH (the absent-command case emits stderr). With no other provider installed, the new if returns success without requesting any lib32 driver. Steam installation then requests an unsatisfied lib32-vulkan-driver, and on the current multilib-before-Omarchy configuration pacman's first eligible provider is lib32-nvidia-utils, which depends on nvidia-utils. The prior head also chose an inappropriate provider because Steam was installed before the helper, but the new helper success now makes the Steam installer report success and launch, rather than abort after Steam installation. Repeating the installer with the same missed detection will not install the intended 32-bit Mesa driver. Distinguish 'nothing detected' from a failed/unsupported detector or ensure a provider explicitly before calling pacman; do not assert every non-NVIDIA GPU is covered.
leads.triage: neutral SendMessage to Opus (followup-1.md); confirmed as behaviour but pre-existing unchanged pattern, same package outcome as merge base, lspci in base; not published; behavioural

leads.summary: Lutris and Battle.net still install umu-launcher before the GPU helper, preserving the unwanted NVIDIA fallback
leads.consequence: On a fresh Intel-only or AMD-only installation with no lib32 Vulkan provider yet, umu-launcher's dependency on lib32-vulkan-driver is resolved by the first pacman provider during the earlier package transaction. With the current multilib-first configuration, this is lib32-nvidia-utils and its nvidia-utils dependency. Both installers only run the GPU helper afterward, when it adds the proper Intel/AMD package too late to prevent the NVIDIA packages. This is an existing ordering problem outside the two changed files and not caused or fixed by this PR; Heroic's package only depends on which and gtk3 in the fetched Omarchy package metadata, so do not extend this finding to Heroic.
leads.triage: corroboration; published as still present; already in Opus final (R1-N1)

leads.summary: Related security PR #9470 conflicts exactly on the new empty-GPU success path
leads.consequence: The branches are diverged (not stacked); a merge-file using #9470's own base has conflict markers at merges/9470.merged:43-49. #9470's proposed final statement `(( ${#PACKAGES[@]} == 0 )) || /usr/bin/omarchy-pkg-add ...` itself returns zero on an empty list, so preserving it does NOT reintroduce this PR's no-GPU exit bug. The conflict still requires a deliberate resolution to preserve #9470's privileged absolute-path call and the helper's success status; selecting only this PR's unqualified omarchy-pkg-add loses #9470's argument/path hardening. Do not merge conflict markers or a duplicate package-add. GitHub currently marks #9470 CONFLICTING against current base tip.
leads.triage: corroboration; draft PR, its tail also exits 0; not published; already in Opus final (related PRs)

leads.summary: Open PR #7583 would change the default provider behind the Steam comment to the legacy NVIDIA 580xx package
leads.consequence: If the independent, open #7583 lands with its stated order (Omarchy repository above multilib), then when no lib32 provider is installed the sole Omarchy repo provider, lib32-nvidia-580xx-utils, precedes Arch multilib's lib32-nvidia-utils. Pacman will default to that legacy 32-bit NVIDIA package instead. This does not change successful Intel/AMD detection because the preinstalled provider already satisfies Steam's dependency, but makes the hard-coded 'currently lib32-nvidia-utils' attribution stale and compounds I1 on undetected GPUs. The change is a dependency premise, not a code conflict in Steam; the other PR's package/repo state may change before merge.
leads.triage: context for 'currently' wording; not published; already in Opus final

leads.summary: Concurrent PR #8875 overlaps the same Steam reorder and requires deduplication
leads.consequence: The heads diverged. Merging #8875's Steam diff against this PR's head produces a conflict at merges/8875.merged:14-24; naively keeping both insertion blocks runs omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32 twice before Steam, repeating PCI detection and package-presence scans (the second package transaction is normally skipped by omarchy-pkg-add --needed). A maintainer who merges both needs one GPU helper invocation, one Steam installation, and one order test. #8875's own new test only compares source line positions, so would not catch duplicate helper invocations.
leads.triage: published as overlapping earlier PR; already in Opus final (NEW-1); coordinator verified files and state via gh api

leads.summary: The existing Steam smoke fixture cannot distinguish this PR's installation order from the broken baseline
leads.consequence: The unchanged fixture replaces the GPU helper with an unconditional exit 0 and checks only that Steam eventually launches. Reverting Steam's two calls to the baseline order is a plausible regression that still passes this test: both the base and head copies pass in the sandbox. Add one assertion of the calls' order using logged fake package helper, and a no-GPU real-helper status case so the new if regression is visible; this is a targeted weakness, not a generic demand for more tests.
leads.triage: test-only, no demonstrated failing-baseline test; not published; close to Opus NEW-3

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12569#issuecomment-5826857310) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12569#issuecomment-5836613479). Checked revision: `65883c38`.

**Verified:** The no-GPU exit status finding is resolved, and the comment wording note is resolved. The earlier Verified results still hold at this head and on the current `quattro` tip with this change applied. No regressions were found in the helper's callers or in the failure path.

| Earlier item | Status at `65883c38` |
|---|---|
| Steam not installed when no GPU is detected | Resolved |
| Code comment names the provider without "currently" | Resolved |
| `umu-launcher` ordering in Lutris and Battle.net (outside this PR) | Still present, deferred by the author |

### No-GPU exit status: resolved

`bin/omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32` now ends with the same `if` block as `install/hardware/vulkan.sh`, so an empty package list leaves the helper with exit status 0. On simulated systems with no detected GPU (virtio, QXL, VMware and an NVIDIA Kepler card), the helper exits 1 at `4c5f363d` and 0 at `65883c38`. The Steam installer on the virtio and Kepler systems:

```text
4c5f363d:  gpu-lib32 exits 1 -> script stops, Steam not installed
65883c38:  gpu-lib32 exits 0 -> pkg-add steam -> launch step runs, installer exits 0
```

The author's claim about the other installers also holds: Lutris, Heroic and Battle.net now continue past the helper step on the virtio and Kepler systems and exit 0, where before they stopped with exit 1. With a GPU detected, the helper requests the same packages at every revision tested. When `omarchy-pkg-add` fails, the helper still returns that status and every caller stops right after it.

On undetected hardware, Steam still pulls in `nvidia-utils` and `lib32-nvidia-utils`, exactly as before this PR. The fallback provider mentioned earlier was optional and was not adopted, so this is not a regression.

### Overlapping earlier PR #8875

Open PR #8875 ("Install lib32 GPU drivers before Steam", which says it fixes #8856), opened before this one, makes the same reorder in `bin/omarchy-install-gaming-steam` but does not change the helper. At its head `79c49c46`, the Steam installer still exits 1 before installing Steam when no GPU is detected. The two PRs conflict in `bin/omarchy-install-gaming-steam`, so only one can merge as is.

**Suggested change:** Reference #8856 in this PR's description. Also mention there that `omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32` now exits 0 when no GPU is detected, which also lets Lutris, Heroic and Battle.net finish on such systems. The description currently covers only the line swap.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit, every caller of `omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32`, and pacman 7.1.0 provider selection. The real Omarchy scripts ran in an isolated sandbox with package, sudo, hardware-probe and launch commands stubbed, against synthetic `lspci`/sysfs data, at the previous head, this head, the current `quattro` tip and `quattro` with this change. Package outcomes come from real `pacman -Sp` resolution against current Omarchy-stable and Arch repository databases with synthetic installed-package databases. PR #8875's head ran in the same sandbox. No real hardware, real package installation or Vulkan runtime behavior was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
